a_sizeAndScaling.description: The pure arithmetic in DungeonFortress.Presentation.HudFontSizes: the ordering rule (tooltip body not smaller than the button label) and the scaling rule (ScaledSize multiplies by UiScale). Both are provable without the engine, per ADR 0011.

mutants.name: a-i: tooltip body reverted to its pre-Issue-#127 size
mutants.change: HudFontSizes.cs: public const int TooltipBodyFontSize = ButtonLabelFontSize; -> public const int TooltipBodyFontSize = ButtonLabelFontSize - 1;
mutants.result: FAILED: 4 of 7 (The_tooltip_body_is_not_smaller_than_the_button_label_it_explains plus 3 Scaled_size_grows_exactly_with_UI_scale cases, whose expected literals no longer match the mutated constant)

mutants.name: a-ii: ScaledSize stops applying UiScale
mutants.change: HudFontSizes.cs: return (int)Math.Round(authoredSize * uiScale, MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero); -> return authoredSize;
mutants.result: FAILED: 3 of 7 (A_larger_UI_scale_never_produces_a_smaller_physical_size, plus 2 Scaled_size_grows_exactly_with_UI_scale cases at 1.5 and 2.0 — the 1.0 case still passes by coincidence, since authoredSize == ScaledSize(authoredSize, 1.0))

a_sizeAndScaling.note: After each mutant, src/DungeonFortress.Presentation/HudFontSizes.cs was restored from a byte-for-byte backup (.artifacts/HudFontSizes.cs.orig, diffed with `diff` to confirm identity) and the full `dotnet test` (599 tests across DomainMcp.Tests, Presentation.Tests, Simulation.Tests) was re-run green before continuing.

b_guardInclusion.description: Whether the HUD readability guard actually measures the tooltip, proven the same way the project already proves the legend guard is alive: a CLI regression flag that shrinks the thing being measured and requires the engine to exit 1. This mutant doubles as checkpoint 3's guard-liveness proof.
b_guardInclusion.mechanism: Main.cs: new CLI flag --smoke-hud-tooltip-readability-regression (parsed next to the existing --smoke-hud-readability-regression), calling InjectHudTooltipReadabilityRegression(), which finds the persistent tooltip readability sample Main.CreateControlStrips keeps (_tooltipReadabilitySample, an invisible child of _hudRoot built by HudButton.MakeAuthoredTooltip) and sets its body label's font_size override to 4 — the same magnitude InjectHudReadabilityRegression already uses for a legend row.

result.message: HUD text is unreadable in 7 place(s): 'Label[TooltipBody]' is drawn at 4 physical pixels on frame 1280x720 at UI scale 1, under the 8 px floor; ... (6 more frame/UiScale pairs) ... Text that formally fits its rectangle can still be too small to read, which is what Issue #86 measured at 8-15 physical pixels.

b_guardInclusion.interpretation: The guard rejects the mutated tooltip at 7 of the 12 SupportedFrameMatrix entries (every frame whose automatic UiScale keeps the mutated 4px body under the 8px floor). Before Issue #127, no CLI flag and no guard measurement could have produced this failure at all, because the tooltip did not appear in HudTextSizes() / hudReadability.texts — this is the concrete difference the fix makes, not merely the number 4 being small.
